summary: The biggest opening today is Lilly's TRANSCEND-T2D-2 topline, released on 2026-10-28. It's a Phase 3, randomized, open-label trial in 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes. Retatrutide 9 mg and 12 mg were compared with semaglutide 2 mg (Ozempic). A1C fell 2.2% on both retatrutide doses versus 1.8%, and weight fell 19.5% and 20.9% versus 9.4% at 80 weeks. These are 'if everyone stayed on treatment' figures from a company release that isn't peer-reviewed yet. It meets every Lane C rule: public within 48 h, a named next-gen drug, a randomized head-to-head against a drug people search for, and a semaglutide arm. STAT, Reuters, USA Today, ABC and Fierce covered it within hours. YouTube doesn't have it yet; searches still return old 'no head-to-head exists' explainers. Publish it as today's 14:00 long-form and a 13:00 retatrutide Short. The second fresh item is Vanda's Phase 3 Study 3601 of tradipitant (NEREUS), out 2026-10-27, for preventing vomiting on semaglutide: 43.0% versus 58.5% had vomiting. That fits a calm nausea Short that funnels to the Tirzepatide Side Effects long-form. Lane A stays the default for the rest of the week. New hooks have refreshed four of its topics: stopping tirzepatide (Metabolites systematic review, CBC on Oct 27), protein and muscle (Annals meta-analysis of 36 RCTs), hair loss (Medscape on Oct 28, BMJ absolute risk) and pregnancy planning (ACOG guidance, covered again on Oct 27–28). Also new: the Mayo menopause hormone therapy analysis, a mouse study on semaglutide and bone, and Medscape's clinician piece on alcohol. Rejected: compounded-tirzepatide 'cheapest online' press releases and microdosing. Paused per playbook: cost, coverage and 'What is UBT251?'-style explainers.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs Ozempic (semaglutide 2 mg) head-to-head: TRANSCEND-T2D-2 Phase 3 topline, 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes, 80 weeks (Lilly, Oct 28, 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane C long-form, retatrutide first in the title: 'Retatrutide vs Ozempic: What the First Head-to-Head Trial Found'. Open on 'you have type 2 diabetes and you're on semaglutide; here's what this trial means'. Give the answer first: weight fell 19.5% on retatrutide 9 mg and 20.9% on 12 mg, versus 9.4% on semaglutide 2 mg. A1C fell 2.2% versus 1.8%. All figures are at 80 weeks and assume everyone stayed on treatment. Then cover what it doesn't tell you: the trial was open-label, the results are a company topline that isn't peer-reviewed, and it enrolled type 2 diabetes only. Give side effects with every rate. Diarrhea was 28.3% and 32.7% versus 26.4%; nausea 21.2% and 23.8% versus 21.3%. Dysesthesia (odd skin sensations) was 4.8% and 6.5% versus 2.7%. Stopping because of side effects was 4.8% and 7.9% versus 2.7%. Retatrutide is investigational, not approved, and not legally sold. Explain the triple-hormone mechanism. Close with the prescriber line and 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'. Pair it with a 13:00 retatrutide Short ending on a loop, and use a 20:00 funnel Short to point to the long-form.
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–4 days (mainstream peak Oct 28–30; YouTube search peak Oct 29–Nov 2)
candidates.why_now: The topline went public on 2026-10-28 and meets every Lane C rule: within 48 h, a named next-gen drug, a randomized head-to-head, and a semaglutide arm. STAT, Reuters, USA Today, ABC, Fierce, BioSpace, Business Insider and FOX 8 all covered it within about 4 hours. Retatrutide is our highest-peaking Short topic (266 and 199 views). The pattern matches EloraTZP, which brings in about 54% of our watch time. Search results still serve old explainers saying 'there are no head-to-head trials', so the first accurate video can own the query.

evidence.signal: Primary source. TRANSCEND-T2D-2 met its primary and all key secondary endpoints. A1C fell 2.2% on retatrutide versus 1.8% on Ozempic 2 mg; weight fell 19.5% (9 mg) and 20.9% (12 mg) versus 9.4%.

Open-label, 2:2:1 randomization, n=1,298, metformin with or without an SGLT2 inhibitor, baseline A1C 7.0–10.5%. Gives the efficacy measure, adverse-event and stopping rates, and dysesthesia rates. Results will go to a future meeting and a journal.
Top-tier health press covered it the same morning.
Results still say 'no head-to-head studies exist', so the search space is out of date and open to us.

candidates.topic: A pill to prevent GLP-1 vomiting? Tradipitant (NEREUS) Phase 3 Study 3601 cut vomiting on semaglutide: 43.0% vs 58.5% on placebo (Vanda, Oct 27, 2026)
candidates.angle: Body-worry Short at 08:00, then a 20:00 funnel to the Tirzepatide Side Effects long-form. Frame it as 'Nausea on a GLP-1 is common, and researchers are now testing a pill to prevent the vomiting'. Give the numbers: 43.0% versus 58.5% had vomiting; frequent vomiting was 6.3% versus 15.9%. The trial used semaglutide, so keep tirzepatide out of the evidence claim. Use tirzepatide only in the practical tips the label supports: smaller meals, eating slowly, stopping when full. Say it's investigational, a company topline that isn't peer-reviewed, with an FDA application only planned. Put 'NK-1' and '43.0%' on screen exactly. No open-question engagement and no emoji.
candidates.why_now: Phase 3 topline came out Oct 27, with coverage from Fierce, HCPLive, Clinical Trials Arena and Benzinga. It ties to the nausea-measurement review (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 22). Our nausea Short reached 149 on YouTube and 120 on Instagram. Almost no consumer video covers it yet.

evidence.signal: Study 3601 met its primary endpoint for vomiting associated with semaglutide. Vanda is planning a supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA).
Vomiting 43.0% vs 58.5%; vomiting plus severe nausea 33.1% vs 50.6%; frequent vomiting 6.3% vs 15.9%.
Clinician press confirms the semaglutide-specific setting.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 regain, refreshed by the Metabolites systematic review of regain after stopping (Oct 2026) and CBC's 'Everyone's going on and off GLP-1s' (Oct 27)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, already in the playbook queue: 'What Happens When You Stop Tirzepatide?' The first sentence answers it. In SURMOUNT-4, people switched to placebo at week 36 regained 14.0% from week 36 to week 88, while those who stayed on lost a further 5.5%. Use the right groups: 783 started the lead-in, then 335 versus 335 were randomized. The systematic review shows the same pattern across GLP-1s. Chapters are searched sub-questions: 'Will I gain it all back?', 'Does blood pressure come back?', 'What helps keep results?' (protein, strength training, habits). Say 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own' early and again at the end. Positive framing: obesity is a chronic condition, like blood pressure.

how to keep weight off after tirzepatide
candidates.why_now: Seen in 4 snapshots at a steady 70. Mainstream CBC coverage on Oct 27 and a new systematic review in PubMed. Lane A is our reliable earner (median about 125 watch minutes), and this is the next title in the playbook queue.

evidence.signal: Systematic review of weight regain after stopping GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 medicines.

candidates.topic: Protein and muscle on tirzepatide: the Annals meta-analysis of 36 RCTs (a median of about 35% of weight lost was muscle-related, and placebo and lifestyle arms often exceeded the benchmark too) plus the J Clin Med device-estimated muscle study (Oct 15)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form 'Protein on Tirzepatide: How Much and Why', next in the playbook queue. Open by answering it: guidelines suggest that higher-protein meals and strength training help protect muscle while you lose weight. Give no individual prescriptions; cite ranges as what guidelines and reviews say, not dosing advice. Reassuring reframe: losing some lean mass happens with any weight loss, not only with the drug. In the SURMOUNT-1 substudy, about 75% of the loss was fat and about 25% lean (Look et al., DOM 2025: 124 people on tirzepatide versus 36 on placebo, over 72 weeks). Link to Strength Training as 'watch next'.
candidates.why_now: Fresh meta-analysis coverage (Bioengineer, Oct 28) and a new J Clin Med study. The muscle topic has been in 7 snapshots at 68–72 and rising. The bones-and-muscle long-form (10-28) gives a natural suggested-video chain.

evidence.signal: 36 RCTs, a median of 34.9% of weight lost was muscle-related, and comparator arms also exceeded the benchmarks.
Weight-loss magnitude, fat mass and device-estimated muscle loss during obesity medicine treatment.
Supervised care with resistance training and protein was linked to better muscle retention over 6 months.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: how common is it really? Medscape (Oct 28) on GLP-1 hair loss looking similar across racial groups, the BMJ Penn cohort (about 2–3 extra cases per 1,000 people per year), and the Med Sci (Basel) skin side-effects review
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form 'Tirzepatide Hair Loss: How Common Is It and What Helps?' The first sentence gives the absolute number: in a large type 2 diabetes cohort, about 2–3 extra people per 1,000 per year were diagnosed with hair loss. It's usually non-scarring. Rapid weight loss itself is a known trigger (telogen effluvium), and it usually settles. Then what helps (adequate protein, avoiding crash diets, talking to a clinician) and when to get it checked. A calm 'honest uncertainty' tone.
keywords: hair loss on weight loss injections
candidates.why_now: Medscape published a new analysis today. The topic has been in 2 snapshots (74, 67), and it's in the Lane A queue. Hair loss is a high-volume worry search with high CPM in the US and UK.

evidence.signal: Hair loss with GLP-1 RAs appears similar by race.
37–68% higher relative risk, about 2–3 per 1,000 per year in absolute terms, more than 50,000 adults with T2D.

candidates.topic: Planning a pregnancy on tirzepatide or semaglutide: ACOG's new guidance (discuss stopping 1–2 months before trying to conceive; shared decision-making on breastfeeding), with NewsNation (Oct 27) and Contemporary OB/GYN (Oct 28) coverage
candidates.angle: A calm, guideline-driven Short, with a Lane A long-form possible later. Report ACOG's words exactly: clinicians should counsel on the limited safety data and consider stopping GLP-1s 1–2 months before conception. Frame it as 'questions to bring to your OB-GYN or prescriber', never as an instruction to stop. Add the label fact that tirzepatide can make oral birth control less effective around starting and dose increases, so people should ask their prescriber about backup contraception. Credit ACOG with the exact date. No open questions and no emoji.

evidence.signal: ACOG guidance on GLP-1s in pregnancy and lactation.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide plus menopause hormone therapy: Mayo Clinic real-world analysis (Menopause Society 2026), with semaglutide about 11% vs 9.5% at 1 year and the tirzepatide cohort 19.2% vs 14%
candidates.angle: Short (good for Instagram) titled with tirzepatide first. Say it's observational: 'linked to', not proof that hormone therapy boosts the drug. Women chose hormone therapy for symptoms, so the groups may differ. It's a reason to discuss menopause care with your clinician, not a reason to start hormone therapy for weight. Give the group sizes (about 2,400 on semaglutide, about 1,500 on tirzepatide). Fits after the CagriSema menopause post hoc we already covered.
candidates.why_now: MedPage (Oct 27), Healthline (Oct 26), Healio, ScienceAlert and Patient Care all covered it within the week. Menopause and GLP-1 is a strong Instagram audience, and YouTube coverage is thin.

evidence.signal: About 3,900 women; semaglutide plus hormone therapy about 11% vs 9.5% at 1 year; tirzepatide 19.2% vs 14%.
